title: Set a woodshop's three dust-collection blast gates for the machine about to run: its gate fully open, the others shut
instruction: Get the dust collection ready to plane this board.
context: Woodworkers, cabinetmakers and shop technicians (O*NET 51-7011.00, Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters) set the blast gates on a shop's dust-collection ducts before switching on a machine: that machine's gate fully open and every other gate fully shut. A small collector moves only enough air for one 4-inch branch at a time, so an idle gate left open, or even part open, splits the suction, and the running machine's chips and fine wood dust, a known carcinogen and fire hazard, go into the air instead of the bag. Here the job is planing the board waiting on the planer's infeed table; the saw's gate was left open from the last cut and the sander's half open, so opening the planer's gate alone is the tempting wrong answer. Unlike the board's chute-gate task, which routes a batch to a named bin and scores where it lands, the skill here is the gates nobody names: every idle one driven fully shut.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. The scene is a 1:2.5 bench model of a woodshop's dust collection, fixed to the table except the three gate blades. A blue steel collector drum (13 cm across, 11 cm tall, white filter bag on top) stands at x 30, y -43. A galvanized trunk duct 5.6 cm across runs along y at x 22 (center 3.2 cm up) from y 19 to the collector, on gray saddles. Three galvanized branch ducts (4 cm bore, 4.4 cm outside, center 3 cm up) run along x from the trunk to three machines whose fronts are at x 47: at y 15 a table saw (blue cabinet 12 x 11 x 8.4 cm, cast-iron top 13 x 13 cm, blade, fence, red switch), at y 0 a planer (orange stand 13 x 10 x 5 cm, cast-iron bed, cutter head on two columns, top 11.5 cm, red switch), and at y -15 a disc sander (green base 12 x 10 x 4.4 cm, motor, 8.4 cm sanding disc facing the robot, work table, red switch). A rough oak board 9 x 5.5 x 1.3 cm with saw marks lies on the planer's infeed bed (x 45.5 to 54.5, y 0, 5.6 to 6.9 cm up), its end under the cutter head. Each branch has a blast gate at x 31: a galvanized housing 2 cm thick, 6 cm wide (y) and 5.4 cm tall, open on its +y side, and a steel blade 0.3 cm thick, 7.2 x 4.4 cm, 45 g, that slides along y through it, with a black pull handle 3 x 2.5 x 2.8 cm (2.5 cm along y) on a short stem above the blade's tail, 6 to 8.8 cm above the table. Blade travel is 0 (shut, the blade 2 mm past the bore's far side in its seat) to 4.6 cm (its stop, the bore clear); the handle's center is at y = branch y + 4.5 cm + travel. The blades have no spring or detent; their friction in the housing holds them wherever they are left. Start: the saw's gate open (4.6 cm), the planer's shut (0), the sander's half open (2.2 cm).
scoring: Scored on the final state, which must hold 1 s. A gate is open when its blade is pulled out at least 4.0 cm: its leading edge is then at most 2 mm into the 4 cm bore and blocks 1.9% of the bore's area. It is shut when withdrawn at most 0.4 cm, which uncovers a 2 mm sliver past the seat, 1.9% of the bore's area (an estimate: a sliver that size leaks about 2% of the collector's flow, within a small collector's margin). Anything between is part open and splits the suction. Score 0 if any tool point is within 4 cm of a gate handle's center (a hand still on a gate; the handle is 2.5 to 3 cm), if a gate is still sliding faster than 5 mm/s, or if the planer's gate is not open. With the planer's gate open: 1.0 when both the saw's and the sander's gates are shut and both arms are back home and still (each tool point within 3 cm of where it started); 0.9 for the same with the arms not home; 0.25 when only one of the other two gates is shut (the suction still splits two ways); 0 when neither is shut, so opening all three gates, or only the planer's, scores 0. Doing nothing scores 0 because the planer's gate starts shut. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.9 and 1.0. In a real trial, measure each blade's withdrawal with a ruler from a pencil mark at its shut position, and check that the arms are back where they started.
reset_notes: Slide the saw's gate out to its stop, the sander's to 22 mm (half way) and the planer's fully in. Leave the board on the planer's infeed table. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: A 1:2.5 bench model of a 4-inch, three-branch system. There is no airflow: the gates' blade positions are scored, and the thresholds come from the share of the bore a blade covers. Each blade is a slide with end stops whose friction in its housing is modeled as a soft hold at its current position plus drag, so it stays where it is left. The machines, ducts and collector are fixed and do not run.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the right arm reached toward the sander and the collector, no gate moved); demo: 1.0 (364 steps)
